text: Summarize the plot of a story where a detective investigates a murder in a locked room, uncovers three suspects, and reveals the culprit through a discrepancy in their alibis.
Write a Python function that takes a list of integers and returns the second largest unique value, handling edge cases like duplicates and lists shorter than two elements.
Compare the trade-offs between eager and lazy evaluation in programming languages, and explain when each approach tends to produce more predictable performance.

I'm designing a hardware-aware inference router that has to choose between three tiers -- an on-device phone model, a laptop NPU model, and a large cloud model -- for every incoming prompt, and I want you to walk me through, step by step, first how to estimate the difficulty of a prompt without running any of the candidate models, second how to translate that difficulty estimate into a calibrated routing decision given measured per-device pass rates, third how to handle the case where the cheap tier's answer turns out to be wrong despite a favorable difficulty estimate, and finally how all of this should change depending on whether the optimization goal is minimizing latency, energy, or dollar cost.

Analyze the following scenario and identify every logical inconsistency: a shipping company promises next-day delivery for all orders placed before 5pm local time, charges a flat rate regardless of distance, guarantees full refunds for any late package, and claims to be carbon neutral because it plants one tree per shipment, then explain what additional information you would need to determine whether the carbon-neutral claim is actually defensible under a full lifecycle accounting of the shipping emissions.
